extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: We collect dense annotations of objects, attributes, and relationships within each image to leam these models.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and veried entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The rst release of the Visual Genome dataset uses 108 ;249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M (Thomee et al., 2016) and MS-COCO (Lin et al., 2014).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: First, we lowercase, lemmatize, and strip excess whitespace from all attributes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: When a new image is added to the crowdsourcing pipeline with no annotations, it is sent to a worker who is asked to draw three bounding boxes and write three descriptions for the region enclosed by each box.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All components of the dataset except objects are veried using majority voting. Majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) involves three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The majority of our workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old. Our youngest contributor was 18 years old and the oldest was 68 years old. We also had a near-balanced split of 54:15% male and 45 :85% female workers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Our dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer models for comprehensive scene understanding.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Visual Genome was collected and veried entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The rst release of the Visual Genome dataset uses 108 ;249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M (Thomee et al., 2016) and MS-COCO (Lin et al., 2014).

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: For both experiments, we follow a similar data pre-processing pipeline. First, we lowercase, lemmatize, and strip excess whitespace from all attributes.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: When a new image is added to the crowdsourcing pipeline with no annotations, it is sent to a worker who is asked to draw three bounding boxes and write three descriptions for the region enclosed by each box.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) as our primary source of annotations.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: All components of the dataset except objects are veried using majority voting. Majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) involves three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) involves three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: The majority of our workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old. Our youngest contributor was 18 years old and the oldest was 68 years old. We also had a near-balanced split of 54:15% male and 45 :85% female workers.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we also use Stanford's dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) to extract nouns automatically and send them to the workers as suggestions.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Our dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as Figure 13 shows; however, they are quite diverse overall

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this paper, we introduce the Visual Genome dataset with the aim of training and benchmarking the next generation of computer models for comprehensive scene understanding.
